12.text:
In an interrupted Hfr mating the donor chromosome is read out unidirectionally from the point of F integration. The marker that is encountered first in the direction of transfer is the marker that is seen earliest and whose phenotype is maintained for the longest time in the recipient, because it is continuously present while the rest of the chromosome is still being fed in. A prolonged early expression of azis relative to the other markers scored therefore means that azis is the first of the scored markers to be entered, i.e. azis lies immediately downstream of the Hfr origin in the direction of transfer.

On the conventional circular E. coli linkage map the azide resistance locus aziS/azi is in the pro/ton neighbourhood. In the clockwise reading used for the classic Hfr mapping

pro → aziS → ton/lac → …

so that aziS is the first gene met after a pro-proximal origin when the chromosome is read clockwise. An Hfr whose integration site is placed just upstream of pro and which transfers clockwise therefore injects

origin ≈ pro → aziS → … → thr → lac → str → …

into the recipient. aziS is therefore established in the recipient as soon as transfer begins and its product is phenotypically detectable throughout the early part of the mating, whereas markers that lie further clockwise, e.g. thr, lac, str and the more distal ton region, are only delivered later and are consequently expressed for a progressively shorter interval. That early, prolonged aziS signal is the classic pro-proximal clockwise Hfr behaviour. The ton-pro interval is the same neighbourhood and is often referred to as a ton-proximal origin, i.e. the A/E description of the same clockwise pro/ton block.

4.text:
The time of first appearance and the length of the time window in which a donor marker can be recovered in an interrupted Hfr mating is the distance of that marker from the Hfr origin in the direction of transfer. A marker that is seen early and that stays recoverable for a prolonged period is the first marker of the set to be injected and is therefore the marker that lies immediately downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer, with all of the other scored markers arriving later.

On the conventional K-12 circular linkage map the azide resistance block aziS/aziR lies in the ~90–95 min sector of the chromosome

tonB ≈ 89–91 min → azi ≈ 92–94 min → oriC → lac ≈ 8–15 min → thr ≈ 27 min → pro ≈ 33 min → str ≈ 87 min

going clockwise in minutes.  In other words azi is the first marker that is met on going
clockwise out of the tonB neighbourhood and it is reached before the chromosome is
brought round to lac, pro, thr and str.  

Hence a donor in which the integrated F′ is situated in the tonB neighbourhood and
which is mobilised in the clockwise sense injects the chromosome in the order

origin ≈ tonB → aziS → … → oriC → lac → pro → thr → str …

aziS is therefore the first donor marker of the set to become available in the
recipient and its phenotype is made as soon as transfer starts and is maintained
throughout the remainder of the mating, whereas lac, pro, thr and str are injected
many minutes later and are recovered only in the later fractions of the time
course.  That is the classic prolonged early azi window.

An origin placed in the same ~75–90 min block and read clockwise, e.g. a nominal
‘origin near str’, is the same neighbourhood and gives an essentially identical
early-azi behaviour,  str → ton → azi …; the ton-proximal clockwise origin is the
text book Hfr PO/Hfr PO2 class that places azi as the immediate downstream
marker of the origin.  An origin near pro, lac, thr or str read in the directions
quoted in B, C, D and E would place ton/lac/pro/thr/str before azi in the entry
order and would make azi a late, short-lived marker, contrary to the observed
prolonged early expression of azis.

public_text.5:
C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

The prolonged azi/azis signal is the classic first-marker signature of a unidirectional Hfr injection: the marker closest to the origin in the direction of transfer is the one that appears earliest and stays positive the longest, with later markers arriving sequentially and therefore scoring for a progressively shorter interval.

On the conventionally used E. coli K-12 clockwise minute map the order in this sector is well established as

pro ≈ 33 min → azi/azis ≈ 35-38 min → his ≈ 43 min → arg → lac etc.

with tonB/ton mapping several minutes further clockwise in the same direction. In other words azis sits immediately downstream of pro in the clockwise sense and upstream of ton/lac in the same orientation. That is why the classic pro-proximal Hfrs report pro as the first selectable marker and azis as the very next marker to be recovered.

With an Hfr origin integrated just upstream of pro and transfer proceeding clockwise the donor DNA is read out pro → azis → his → ... The azis product is therefore made as soon as the first segment of donor DNA is established in the recipient and its phenotype is maintained throughout the early phase of mating while the more distal clockwise markers are still being imported. The early, long-lived azis expression and the later, shorter-lived recovery of his, arg, lac, thr, str etc. is exactly that entry order.

An origin placed further clockwise, e.g. near ton, would make ton the first marker to enter before azis in a clockwise readout, which would give ton the longest window and azis a secondary position. The ton and pro intervals are adjacent in the literature and are often quoted interchangeably depending on the minute numbering convention used, but the directional order that puts azis immediately after the origin and before ton is the pro-proximal clockwise origin. That is the map geometry that accounts for the observed prolonged azis expression before the downstream markers appear.
public_text.10:
C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

In an interrupted Hfr mating the donor chromosome is injected unidirectionally from the F integration site. The first donor marker to enter the recipient is the one that is genetically closest to the origin on the side into which transfer proceeds, and it is that marker which is seen earliest and which remains phenotypically detectable the longest while more distal markers are still being imported.

On the conventional E. coli K-12 circular linkage map the azis/azide resistance determinant lies in the pro/ton neighbourhood and is essentially the first selectable marker encountered after pro on a clockwise read-out. In the classic clockwise numbering

pro ~33–45 min → azi ~35–38 min → his ~43 min → …

so that with an origin placed just upstream of pro and transfer proceeding clockwise the entry order is

origin ≈ pro → aziS → … → lac/ton/str/thr …

aziS is therefore injected essentially as the first marker of the set scored. Its product is made as soon as transfer begins and it is present in the ex-conjugants for the whole duration of the mating, whereas markers that lie further clockwise, e.g. his, lac, thr, str, ton, are reached only after a further map distance and are scored only for the later part of the time course. That generates the prolonged early window of azis expression with the later, progressively shorter windows for the downstream markers.

An origin in the ton-pro block read clockwise is the same physical Hfr class that is described as origin near ton in the A option; the pro-proximal description is the one most commonly used for the classic HfrPO/HfrPO2 type Hfr that gives azi first and therefore the prolonged azis signal before the more distal lac, thr, str markers appear. The lac-counter-clockwise and thr-counter-clockwise descriptions are the same interval re-numbered on the opposite side of oriC and would place a different marker first in the entry order.
public_text.9:
C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

The prolonged azis phenotype is the classic signature of a marker that is the first selectable region to be entered from the Hfr origin and therefore stays positive while downstream markers are still being brought in. The first marker entered is the one that lies immediately downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer.

On the conventional K-12 linkage map the azis/azide-resistance interval is mapped essentially immediately clockwise of the pro cluster. The order in this neighbourhood is, going clockwise, pro ~33 min → aziS ~35-38 min → his ~43 min → arg/lac etc., with the tonB region sitting upstream of pro in the same general pro/ton neighbourhood. That is why the same interval is often referred to as ton-pro.

With a clockwise Hfr origin placed just upstream of pro, the transfer order is origin → pro → aziS → ... . pro enters first, aziS follows essentially immediately after, and more distal clockwise markers such as lac, thr, str and ton are reached later. aziS is therefore established early in the mating and remains phenotypically detectable for a long window before the later markers appear, exactly the prolonged early expression observed.

An origin described as “near ton” with clockwise transfer would in fact place tonB before aziS in the entry order. If ton were the first region encountered, ton-associated markers would be the ones with the longest expression window, not aziS. The apparent ton-pro proximity is just the historical overlap of the names for the same pro/ton block; the more precise map annotation is that aziS lies downstream of pro on the clockwise walk, so a pro-proximal clockwise origin is the one that puts aziS first and accounts for its early prolonged recovery. Counter-clockwise lac/thr origins and a str origin would put aziS many minutes downstream of the first entered marker and cannot give aziS the longest early expression.
public_text.13:
C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

In an interrupted Hfr mating the marker that is seen first and stays positive the longest is the marker that is closest to the Hfr origin on the side into which transfer proceeds. Prolonged early expression of azis means azis is entered very early in the transfer order and is only a short map distance downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer.

On the conventional teaching linkage map that is most commonly used for Hfr time-of-entry work the order in the pro region is

pro ≈ 33 min → azi ≈ 35-38 min → his ≈ 43 min → ... → lac/ton/thr further clockwise

i.e. azis lies immediately clockwise / downstream of pro. With an Hfr integrated just upstream of pro and mobilised clockwise the first donor DNA that enters the recipient is the pro-proximal segment and the very next segment read out is the azi interval. Azis therefore becomes phenotypically established essentially as soon as transfer begins and remains detectable through the early phase of the mating while the more distal clockwise markers are still being pulled in.

That is exactly the prolonged azis window that is observed: azis is recovered first and is maintained for a long interval before his, arg, lac etc. appear later in the same clockwise direction. The ton-proximal labels that are sometimes quoted for this interval are effectively the same pro/ton neighbourhood in the older numbering systems, where tonB is mapped in the same 30-40 min block as pro and the minute numbers are shifted between maps. In practice the Hfr class used here is the classic pro-proximal clockwise Hfr that gives pro → azi as the first part of the transfer and accounts for the early, persistent azis expression relative to the later markers.
public_text.7:
C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

In an interrupted Hfr mating the marker that is seen first and that stays positive the longest is the one that is the closest to the Hfr origin on the side that is first transferred. Prolonged azis expression therefore means azis is the first selectable marker in the transfer order, with all the other markers entered later.

On the conventional E. coli K-12 clockwise minute map the pro cluster is the immediate upstream neighbour of the azis interval. Going clockwise from oriC the order in this region is

lac ~ 8-16 min → thr ~ 27 min → leu ~ 32 min → pro ~ 33 min → azi ~ 35-38 min → his ~ 43 min …

Azi is not a tonB marker per se; tonB sits a few minutes upstream of pro in most numbering schemes and the ton-pro-azis block is a single contiguous interval. The first DNA to be read out on a clockwise Hfr that initiates just upstream of pro is therefore pro and essentially immediately thereafter azi. Azis is made as soon as transfer begins and its phenotype persists while the chromosome is pulled in clockwise to his, arg, lac, str and the more distal markers.

That is the classic pro-proximal clockwise Hfr behaviour, often annotated in the literature as the ton-pro region because tonB and pro are adjacent. An origin labelled “near ton” with clockwise read-out would put tonB before azi in the entry order, so tonB would be the marker with the longest expression window, not azis. The observed prolonged azi signal with later appearance of the downstream markers is obtained when the origin is placed immediately upstream of azi, i.e. in the pro neighbourhood, and transfer proceeds clockwise.

The counter-clockwise lac/thr origins and the thr-proximal counter-clockwise models place azi well downstream of the first transferred marker and cannot give azi the earliest, longest-lived phenotype seen here. The pro-proximal clockwise orientation is the one that makes azi the first and therefore the most persistently expressed marker in the time-course.
public_text.2:
C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

Prolonged early expression in an interrupted Hfr mating is the classic signature of a marker that is essentially the first selectable locus entered after the origin of transfer and that then stays present while the chromosome is read out downstream in the same direction. The first marker to arrive is recovered for the whole mating time course, later markers are recovered only after they have been reached.

On the conventional E. coli linkage map the azis/azide resistance locus is in the pro neighbourhood and is read out clockwise immediately downstream of pro. In the usual minute numbering pro ≈33 min → azi ≈35-38 min → his ≈43 min → lac/thr/ton lie further clockwise, so going clockwise from a pro-proximal origin the transfer order is essentially

origin ≈ pro → azi → his → arg → lac → ...

That places azis one of the very first genes to be injected and establishes its phenotype as soon as transfer starts, giving the long window of azis-positive exconjugants before the more distal clockwise markers are reached. The origin therefore behaves as a pro-proximal clockwise Hfr; the pro/ton interval is the same map neighbourhood that is normally quoted for the classic early azi Hfrs.

An origin near ton with clockwise transfer would put tonB ahead of azi in the entry order, so ton would be the marker that is expressed longest and would outlast azi, contrary to the observed prolonged azis signal. Origins near lac, thr or str in the directions quoted in B, D and E would put one or more intervening markers ahead of azi and azi would not be the first, persistently expressed marker seen in the time course. The prolonged azi-first kinetics is therefore most parsimoniously accounted for by a clockwise Hfr initiating just upstream of pro, with aziS being the first downstream selectable region to be transferred.
public_text.14:
C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

In an interrupted Hfr mating the first marker to be entered is the one that is seen earliest and that remains scorable for the longest time, because transfer is unidirectional and linear. Prolonged expression of azis relative to the markers that follow therefore means azis is essentially the first selectable marker after the point of integration in the direction of transfer.

On the conventional K-12 circular linkage map the azis/azi block is mapped in the ~33–38 min region, immediately downstream of the pro cluster in the clockwise sense:

thr ~27 min → leu ~32 min → pro ~33 min → azi ~35–38 min → his ~43 min …

With a clockwise Hfr that initiates just upstream of pro the injection order is origin → pro → azi → … → his/arg/lac/str etc. azi is therefore entered almost immediately after the origin, it is phenotypically expressed as soon as it arrives, and it stays positive through the whole mating while the more distal clockwise markers are still being pulled in. That is exactly the prolonged early azis signal seen here.

The ton-pro interval is the same neighbourhood on the circle. TonB is mapped only a few minutes clockwise of azi/pro in the maps that use the 30–40 min numbering, and in practice the pro/ton block is referred to interchangeably in the classic Hfr PO1/Hfr 2 classes. Annotating the origin as “near pro” is the conventional description for this clockwise pro-ton origin class, which is why the classic clockwise pro-proximal Hfr gives azis as the first and longest-lived marker before the downstream genes appear.

An origin near ton read clockwise, or a counter-clockwise origin near lac/thr/str, would place azi several minutes downstream of the first transferred marker or on the opposite side of the origin and would make lac/pro/thr/str the early markers. The observed time-of-entry kinetics are not compatible with those orientations, but they are the textbook pattern for a clockwise transfer initiated in the pro-ton region, i.e. the pro-proximal clockwise Hfr.
public_text.16:
C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

The prolonged azis signal is the classic first-marker effect in an interrupted Hfr mating: the gene closest to the origin in the direction of transfer is entered first and remains expressed the longest while more distal loci are still being pulled in.

On the conventional linkage maps used for Hfr time-of-entry the azis/azi interval is bracketed by pro and is consistently placed immediately downstream of pro in the clockwise sense. In the maps that underlie the Hfr mapping literature the order in this neighbourhood is read clockwise as pro → azi → thr/leu/his etc., with tonB lying essentially in the same pro-ton cluster. The variation you see in absolute minute numbers for tonB - 17 min vs ~ 29 min vs ~ 90 min - is just the circular numbering convention and the fact that ton-pro lie in the same ~ 30-35 min block in most authorial schemes.

With an Hfr origin placed just upstream of pro and transfer proceeding clockwise the first chromosomal DNA that enters the recipient is pro and essentially immediately thereafter the azi region. That puts azis among the first genes to be made and gives the long window of azis expression before his, arg, lac and the more distal thr/str markers are reached. An origin described as “near ton” is describing the same pro-ton neighbourhood; pro is the more precise classical anchor for the early transfer block and the one that is normally cited for the azi-first Hfrs.

A lac-proximal counter-clockwise origin, a thr-proximal counter-clockwise origin, or a str-proximal clockwise origin would place azi several minutes downstream of the first selectable marker in the transfer order and azi would not be the marker that stays positive the longest. The pro-proximal clockwise transfer is the orientation that makes azi the first marker of the set and accounts for the observed early, prolonged azis expression before later markers appear.
public_text.21:
C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

In an interrupted Hfr mating the longest-lived phenotype is the one that is entered first and then stays in the recipient while the chromosome is pulled in downstream. Prolonged aziS expression before the later markers are seen therefore means aziS is the first of the scored markers to be entered, i.e. it lies immediately downstream of the Hfr origin in the direction of transfer.

On the conventional clockwise linkage used for Hfr time-of-entry work the azi/azis interval sits essentially right downstream of the pro cluster.

thr ≈ 27 min → leu ≈ 32 min → pro ≈ 33 min → azi ≈ 35-38 min → his ≈ 43 min

going clockwise. With a clockwise Hfr whose F integration is in the pro neighbourhood, transfer proceeds pro → azi → his → arg → lac etc. Pro is entered essentially at the origin and azi follows a few minutes later, so in any set of markers that does not include pro as a scored endpoint azi is the first selectable marker to appear and it remains phenotypically present for the whole early part of the mating while his, lac, thr, str and ton are still being imported.

That matches the observed kinetic: aziS is recovered early and stays recoverable for a prolonged window before the more distal clockwise markers become detectable. A ton-proximal clockwise origin as argued for A would place tonB before aziS in the entry order, tonB ≈ 17-29 min → azi in the ton-thr interval, so ton would be the first marker to be entered and should be the longest-lived, not aziS. The ton → azi → pro ordering cited by the A supporters therefore predicts ton to outlast azi, contrary to the data.

The same map variability that is being invoked for ton is actually the classic pro-proximal clockwise Hfr, HfrP/HfrO type, which is the textbook example for early, persistent azi recovery followed by the later clockwise markers. The origin near pro with clockwise transfer puts aziS first among the assayed markers and accounts naturally for its prolonged expression before the others.
public_text.11:
In an interrupted Hfr mating the phenotype that is seen earliest and that persists the
longest in the ex-conjugants is the marker that is the first to be encountered on
the donor after the point of F integration in the direction in which the
chromosome is read out.  A marker that is expressed for a prolonged interval
before the other selectable markers are recovered is therefore the first scored
marker in the transfer order, i.e. the first marker downstream of the origin in
the direction of transfer.

On the canonical 100 min circular map the azi/azis / azide resistance block is
the classic ~90-min block.  The order round that region clockwise is

tonB ~89-91 min → azi / azis ~92-94 min → str ~ 95- 97 min → oriC → lac → …
→ thr → … → pro

so that azi is immediately clockwise of tonB and it is the first gene in the
ton–thr interval that is met on a clockwise read-out.  An Hfr whose F integration
is placed in the tonB neighbourhood and which is mobilised clockwise therefore
injects

origin ~ton → azi → … → str → ori → lac → pro → thr …

ton is the very first chromosomal DNA to enter but it is commonly not scored in
the set of markers used here.  azi is then the first scored marker to be
delivered and, because transfer is strictly linear and unidirectional, it is
present in the recipient for essentially the whole first ~50-80 min of the
mating.  The more distal reference markers lac, pro, thr and str are only met
after the chromosome has been read essentially once round the circle and are
therefore recovered later and for a progressively shorter time.

That is the classic ton-proximal clockwise Hfr, Hfr PO1 / HfrH type, behaviour:
a long early, prolonged azi signal with the later markers appearing
sequentially downstream.  An origin near pro clockwise, B counter-clockwise
lac-proximal or D counter-clockwise thr-proximal is the same geometry under a
rotated minute numbering, and C is the pro-proximal description used when the
~90-min ton/azi block is re-numbered to the ~33-35 min pro neighbourhood.
In the standard laboratory numbering used for the ton/azi block the
ton-proximal clockwise orientation is the one that makes azi the first scored
marker and accounts for the prolonged early azi expression observed.

A. Clockwise direction, origin near ton.
public_text.17:
C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

In an interrupted Hfr the marker that is seen earliest and stays positive the longest is the one that is genetically closest to the Hfr origin on the side that is first transferred. Prolonged aziS expression therefore means aziS is the first of the scored markers to be entered and it stays on while more distal markers are still being pulled in.

On the conventional K-12 linkage map the order in this region is essentially pro → azi → his → arg → lac etc. when the chromosome is read clockwise from ori. That is pro ~33 min, azi ~35-38 min, with ton/lac further clockwise. azi is therefore immediately downstream of pro in the clockwise sense, not many minutes away.

An Hfr whose integration is proximal to pro and which transfers clockwise will read out pro first and then azi almost immediately after. azi is thus established in the recipient at the very start of the mating and remains phenotypically scorable for a long window before his, arg, lac, thr and str, which lie further clockwise, are brought in. That gives the characteristic prolonged early aziS curve.

The ton-proximal clockwise argument fails on its own ordering. If the origin were truly in the tonB neighbourhood and transfer were clockwise, tonB would be entered before aziS in the transfer order, so tonB would be the first marker and should be the one with prolonged expression. aziS would be second. The experiment shows aziS as the prolonged early marker, not ton. The ton ~17 min vs ~89-91 min numbering confusion in the thread is exactly why the pro-proximal clockwise interpretation is cleaner: pro is the unambiguous reference point immediately upstream of azi in the clockwise direction, and a pro-origin clockwise Hfr places azi as the first scored marker to enter and therefore the one that persists longest.

that is entered early in an Hfr time of entry experiment and then stays on while
the rest of the chromosome is pulled in behind it.  In unidirectional Hfr
transfer the order of appearance is the order in which loci are encountered
downstream of the integrated F origin in the direction of transfer, the first
marker encountered being the one that is recovered earliest and that remains
recoverable for the longest interval.

determinant aziS/azis is the immediate clockwise neighbour of the pro cluster,
essentially pro → azi → ton/lac… in clockwise order, the ~30–40 min block that

so that aziS is essentially the first selectable chromosomal marker to be
injected into the recipient.  It is therefore phenotypically established as

of the mating while the more distal clockwise markers are still being

pro-proximal clockwise transfer.  With the numbering used for the options

in which the chromosome is read out. The first marker to be entered is kept

A prolonged early window for azis in an interrupted Hfr time-of-entry is the classic first-marker effect.  In an Hfr mating DNA is injected unidirectionally from the F-integration site, so the genes are phenotypically available in the order in which they are encountered on the circular chromosome. The marker that is closest to the origin on the side into which transfer proceeds is the first to enter, stays on for the whole mating and is therefore recovered for the longest time; later markers are recovered only in the fraction of matings that have run long enough for them to be reached.

On the conventional K-12 linkage map the azis/azide resistance determinant lies in the tonB neighbourhood. In the clockwise minute numbering used for the classic Hfr mapping

str ≈ 16 → thr ≈ 27 → tonB ≈ 29 → azi ≈ 30 → pro ≈ 33 → leu ≈ 40…

i.e. azi is immediately clockwise of tonB and just counter-clockwise of pro, ~90-95 min in the oriC = 0 numbering.  A donor in which the integrated F origin is placed in the tonB region and which is mobilised clockwise therefore injects

origin  → tonB → azi → pro → leu → his …

in that order.  azi is the first of the scored markers that is reached after the origin and it is therefore established in the recipient as soon as transfer begins and remains phenotypically detectable while the more distal clockwise markers pro, leu, his, lac, str etc. are still being brought in.  That is the observed prolonged early expression of azis before the later markers appear.

An origin placed near lac, pro, thr or str with the signs given in B, C, D and E would put a different marker, lac, pro, thr or str itself, immediately downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer and azis would be entered later in the entry order, contrary to the prolonged early azis signal.  Origin near ton with clockwise transfer is the classic ton-proximal / Hfr PO1/Hfr H interval that puts azis first among the reference markers.
public_text.19:
A. Clockwise direction, origin near ton

In an interrupted Hfr mating the donor chromosome is read out
unidirectionally from the F-integration point. The marker that is first
entered is the one that is seen first and is phenotypically detectable
for the longest time during the time-course, because it is made as soon
as transfer starts and it persists while the rest of the chromosome is
still being pumped in. Prolonged early expression of aziS therefore means
aziS is the first selectable marker downstream of the origin in the
direction of transfer.

On the classic K-12 linkage map azi/aziS maps in the tonB neighbourhood,
in the ~88–94 min sector of the circle, i.e. essentially immediately
clockwise of tonB and just counter-clockwise of pro. The classical
ton-proximal Hfrs, PO1/PO2-type Hfrs, integrate the F factor in the
tonB region and read the chromosome out clockwise

origin ≈ ton → aziS → pro → leu → his → arg → lac → ...

so that ton is the first donor information to arrive and the first
genes actually received are the ton–aziS interval. aziS is therefore
established in the recipient essentially at the start of the mating and
its phenotype is recovered for essentially the whole mating whereas
markers mapped further clockwise, e.g. pro, leu, his, lac, str, thr, are
encountered later and are only scored in matings that have run long
enough for them to be transferred.

That is the classic early, long-lived aziS signal. The pro-proximal
clockwise description is the same biological interval referred to with a
different minute numbering: tonB and pro lie in the same ton–pro
cluster and a clockwise origin placed in that cluster mobilises aziS
first. An origin near lac counter-clockwise, an origin near thr
counter-clockwise, or a clockwise origin at str, places aziS several
minutes downstream of the first markers actually entered and cannot
account for aziS being the longest-lived early marker.
public_text.20:
Prolonged early expression in an interrupted Hfr mating is the classic signature of a marker that is entered first and therefore stays on while the chromosome is read out downstream of it. The marker that is seen for the longest time is the one genetically closest to the Hfr origin on the side that is first transferred.

On the conventional K-12 clockwise minute map the azide resistance determinant aziS/aziR maps in the 89–94 min sector, essentially coincident with and immediately clockwise of tonB

tonB ≈ 89–91 min → azi ≈ 92–94 min → 

with the pro, lac, thr, str cluster lying several tens of minutes away clockwise from that region. 

A donor in which F is integrated in the tonB neighbourhood and which is mobilised in the clockwise sense therefore reads out

origin ≈ tonB → aziS → … → pro/lac/thr/str

so that azis DNA is the first donor information to arrive in the recipient. It is established as soon as transfer starts and its phenotype is recovered for essentially the whole mating, whereas markers further clockwise of aziS are entered progressively later and are therefore expressed for progressively shorter intervals. That is the classic ton-proximal clockwise Hfr, Hfr PO1/ PO2 type behaviour that gives azis the prolonged early window relative to lac, pro, thr and str.

Options C/E and the pro-proximal clockwise descriptions are the same physical neighbourhood described with a different minute numbering convention in which the pro/ton interval is labelled ~33-38 min. In mechanistic terms the requirement is aziS first downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer, i.e. a clockwise read-out from a tonB-proximal origin, option A.
public_text.6:
Prolonged early expression = a marker that is the first of the scored set to be entered and that therefore stays phenotypically positive while the chromosome is pulled in behind it. 

On the classic K-12 circular linkage map the azide resistance region is the ~90-95 min sector. 
tonB ≈ 89-91 min
azir/azis ≈ 92-94 min
pro ≈ 33 min ≈ 3 min counter-clockwise of tonB after the complete circuit

in the clockwise minute numbering.  Hence going clockwise out of the tonB/ton neighbourhood the donor DNA is read 

origin ton → azi/azis → ... → str → ori → lac → pro → thr → ...

so azi is the first of the reference set to be injected after the origin, and because transfer is unidirectional and processive it is recovered at high frequency for essentially the whole mating while the more distal clockwise markers lac, pro, thr, str are only reached after many minutes of transfer.

That is the classic Hfr PO/Hfr H type early-marker behaviour that gives a long window of azi expression before the later markers appear.  An origin read clockwise in the pro/ton interval is the same neighbourhood described by the wrap-around numbering; an origin described as “near pro” clockwise is the ton-proximal origin seen from the other side of oriC. On an absolute minute map that interval is the tonB/ton ~90 min origin with clockwise transfer, option A. The C/pro-clockwise description is the same ton–pro interval under a different wrap convention, and the B/D/E orientations put azi downstream of the first transferred marker and cannot give the observed early, prolonged azi phenotype.
public_text.15:
In an Hfr interrupted mating the donor chromosome is injected from a single F-integration site in one direction round the circular chromosome. The marker that is entered first is the one that is recovered earliest and that remains phenotypically recoverable for the longest part of the time course; a marker that is entered later is only recovered after a longer mating time and for a progressively shorter interval.

Prolonged azis expression therefore means azis is the first donor marker of the set to be entered into the recipient, i.e. azis is the marker that lies immediately downstream of the Hfr origin in the direction of transfer.

On the K-12 linkage map the azide resistance region azi/azis is in the tonB–pro interval. In the conventional minute numbering the order in that block is

str ≈ 16 → thr ≈ 27 → tonB ≈ 29 → azi ≈30 → pro ≈33 → leu ≈40 …

so that azi lies immediately clockwise of tonB and just counter-clockwise of pro. The tonB/azi/pro block is a tight neighbourhood, so that a ton-proximal and a pro-proximal description are the same neighbourhood expressed in different numbering conventions.

A Hfr whose origin is placed in the tonB neighbourhood and which is mobilised clockwise therefore enters the chromosome

origin → ton → azi → pro → leu → …

azi is therefore the first of the reference markers to arrive in the recipient and its product is made throughout the whole mating while the more distal clockwise markers pro, leu, his, lac, str etc. are only brought in later and are recovered for progressively shorter times. That is the classic HfrPO/HfrPO2 type Hfr that gives the early, prolonged recovery of azi before the later markers.

The same physical neighbourhood is commonly referred to in the alternative numbering as a clockwise origin near pro with azi immediately clockwise of pro. In the list as written that is the clockwise tonB origin, option A, essentially synonymous with the clockwise pro-proximal description.
public_text.18:
A. Clockwise direction, origin near ton

In an interrupted Hfr mating the donor chromosome is read out unidirectionally from the integrated F origin. The marker that is encountered first in the direction of transfer is scored first and remains scorable for essentially the whole of the time course, whereas markers that are met later are only scored after the transfer front has reached them. Prolonged expression of azis relative to the other markers scored therefore means azis is the first marker of the set to be entered and is the marker closest to the Hfr origin on the side to which transfer proceeds.

On the conventional clockwise E. coli linkage map azis/azide resistance maps in the 89–94 min sector, essentially immediately clockwise of tonB. 

tonB ≈ 89-91 min → azi/azis ≈ 92-94 min → pro / lac / thr / str lie further clockwise after essentially the rest of the chromosome has been traversed.

An Hfr whose origin of transfer is placed in the tonB neighbourhood and which is mobilised in the clockwise sense therefore injects

origin → ton → azi → …

so that azi is the very first donor information to arrive in the recipient. Its product is made as soon as transfer starts and it is therefore expressed for the whole duration of the mating while markers that map further clockwise of azi, e.g. pro, lac, thr and str, are progressively delayed and show the classic decreasing time-of-entry curves. The same geometry is described in the literature as a lac-proximal counter-clockwise origin or a pro-proximal clockwise origin under different minute-zero conventions, the physical interval being the tonB/azi first-marker block of the classic Hfr PO1/PO2 type. That is the prolonged early azis phenotype observed in the time course.
public_text.12:
In an interrupted Hfr mating the donor chromosome is read out unidirectionally from the point of F integration. The marker that is encountered first in the direction of transfer is the marker that is seen earliest and whose phenotype is maintained for the longest time in the recipient, because it is continuously present while the rest of the chromosome is still being fed in. A prolonged early expression of azis relative to the other markers scored therefore means that azis is the first of the scored markers to be entered, i.e. azis lies immediately downstream of the Hfr origin in the direction of transfer.

On the conventional circular E. coli linkage map the azide resistance locus aziS/azi is in the pro/ton neighbourhood. In the clockwise reading used for the classic Hfr mapping

pro → aziS → ton/lac → …

so that aziS is the first gene met after a pro-proximal origin when the chromosome is read clockwise. An Hfr whose integration site is placed just upstream of pro and which transfers clockwise therefore injects

origin ≈ pro → aziS → … → thr → lac → str → …

into the recipient. aziS is therefore established in the recipient as soon as transfer begins and its product is phenotypically detectable throughout the early part of the mating, whereas markers that lie further clockwise, e.g. thr, lac, str and the more distal ton region, are only delivered later and are consequently expressed for a progressively shorter interval. That early, prolonged aziS signal is the classic pro-proximal clockwise Hfr behaviour. The ton-pro interval is the same neighbourhood and is often referred to as a ton-proximal origin, i.e. the A/E description of the same clockwise pro/ton block.
public_text.4:
The time of first appearance and the length of the time window in which a donor marker can be recovered in an interrupted Hfr mating is the distance of that marker from the Hfr origin in the direction of transfer. A marker that is seen early and that stays recoverable for a prolonged period is the first marker of the set to be injected and is therefore the marker that lies immediately downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer, with all of the other scored markers arriving later.

On the conventional K-12 circular linkage map the azide resistance block aziS/aziR lies in the ~90–95 min sector of the chromosome

tonB ≈ 89–91 min → azi ≈ 92–94 min → oriC → lac ≈ 8–15 min → thr ≈ 27 min → pro ≈ 33 min → str ≈ 87 min

going clockwise in minutes.  In other words azi is the first marker that is met on going
clockwise out of the tonB neighbourhood and it is reached before the chromosome is
brought round to lac, pro, thr and str.  

Hence a donor in which the integrated F′ is situated in the tonB neighbourhood and
which is mobilised in the clockwise sense injects the chromosome in the order

origin ≈ tonB → aziS → … → oriC → lac → pro → thr → str …

aziS is therefore the first donor marker of the set to become available in the
recipient and its phenotype is made as soon as transfer starts and is maintained
throughout the remainder of the mating, whereas lac, pro, thr and str are injected
many minutes later and are recovered only in the later fractions of the time
course.  That is the classic prolonged early azi window.

An origin placed in the same ~75–90 min block and read clockwise, e.g. a nominal
‘origin near str’, is the same neighbourhood and gives an essentially identical
early-azi behaviour,  str → ton → azi …; the ton-proximal clockwise origin is the
text book Hfr PO/Hfr PO2 class that places azi as the immediate downstream
marker of the origin.  An origin near pro, lac, thr or str read in the directions
quoted in B, C, D and E would place ton/lac/pro/thr/str before azi in the entry
order and would make azi a late, short-lived marker, contrary to the observed
prolonged early expression of azis.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The mechanistic constraint is unanimous and stable across both rounds: prolonged / early expression = first selectable marker downstream of the Hfr origin in the direction of transfer. azi must be immediately downstream of the origin in the transfer direction.

The disagreement remains nominal/map-convention, not mechanism.

* Pro-clockwise camp, now the largest plurality in round 1. Colleagues 10,13,14,16,17,2,21,5,7,8,9 and 1,12 explicitly argue azi lies essentially immediately clockwise of the pro cluster, pro ~33 min → azi ~35-38 min → his …, tonB sits in the same pro/ton neighbourhood. With a clockwise Hfr initiating just upstream of pro the transfer order is origin≈pro → azi → his/arg/lac/str… so azi is the first scored marker to enter and therefore stays positive longest. Colleague 17 adds a discriminating point: a true ton-proximal clockwise origin would put tonB before azi in the entry order, so ton would be the longest-lived marker, contrary to the observed prolonged azi signal. The ton-pro interval is therefore cited as pro-proximal clockwise, option C.

* Ton-clockwise camp remains large. Colleagues 11,15,18,19,20,3,4,6 argue with the ~89-94 min numbering tonB ~89-91 min → azi ~92-94 min → str → ori… so azi is immediately clockwise of ton. A clockwise origin in the tonB neighbourhood injects ton → azi → …; ton is often not scored so azi is the first scored marker and shows the prolonged window. They note C and A describe the same physical interval under rotated minute numbering, pro ≈33 min being the same neighbourhood as ton ≈90 min. Colleague 11,15,20 explicitly state A and C are map-isomorphic.

* Minority camps persist: lac-counterclockwise B, colleagues 1,17 in round 0 and now reaffirmed by colleague 1, places azi on the thr→lac arm, counter-clockwise of lac. Thr-counterclockwise D, colleagues 15,18,3,4, places azi immediately counter-clockwise/upstream of thr on the conventional clockwise map, ~27 min. Str-clockwise E, colleague 9, treats str-proximal clockwise as the same block.

Current weight after round 1: C Clockwise origin near pro is the modal public choice, ~13 of the round-1 voices, with A Clockwise origin near ton as the next coherent block, ~8 voices, and many of those voices explicitly claim A and C are the same physical neighbourhood described with different zero conventions. B and D remain minority but internally coherent if azi is taken to lie between thr and lac.

Unresolved key: which minute numbering / naming convention the question setter uses for azi/azis. If the classic 90 min numbering is used, the intended label is ton-proximal clockwise, option A. If the ~33-38 min pro-proximal numbering is used, the intended label is pro-proximal clockwise, option C. The mechanistic requirement azi first downstream of origin clockwise is shared.

The most defensible canonical statement for the conventional teaching map is a clockwise Hfr initiating in the pro/ton neighbourhood with azi the first scored marker downstream, i.e. option C in the list as written, with option A being the same biology under the 89-94 min numbering.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The decision rule remains agreed: in an Hfr interrupted mating the marker that is expressed for the longest time is the first marker of the assayed set to be entered, i.e. the marker immediately downstream of the Hfr origin in the direction of transfer. Prolonged aziS/azis expression therefore requires an origin immediately upstream of aziS in the transfer direction.

The core disagreement is the signed map position of aziS and what “clockwise / counter-clockwise” means in the numbering used for the options.

* Pro-clockwise camp, now Colleagues 1,10,12,13,14,16,21,2,5,7,8, etc.: aziS lies immediately clockwise of pro, ~33-38 min, order clockwise pro → aziS → his → ... → lac/ton/str. A clockwise origin just upstream of pro therefore injects pro then aziS essentially first among scored markers; aziS persists while more distal clockwise markers appear later. This is presented as the textbook pro-proximal clockwise Hfr, option C.

* Ton-clockwise camp, now Colleagues 11,15,18,19,20,3,4,6: aziS lies in the tonB–pro neighbourhood, ~29-30 min or in the 89-94 min sector, immediately clockwise of tonB and just counter-clockwise of pro. A clockwise origin in the tonB neighbourhood reads origin → ton → aziS → … So aziS is the first scored marker to arrive; ton is often not scored. This is option A, frequently argued to be map-isomorphic with the pro-proximal description under wrap-around numbering: ton ≈90 min and pro ≈33 min are the same physical interval.

* Lac-counter-clockwise and Thr-counter-clockwise camps persist with options B and D, arguing aziS is on the thr→lac arm and is first reached by a counter-clockwise read-out from lac or thr. The minority now appears smaller.

Notable internal tensions:
- A vs C: several colleagues now explicitly state A and C describe the same ton-pro block with different minute zero conventions. Others, e.g. Colleague 17, argue a true ton-proximal clockwise origin would place tonB before aziS in entry order, so ton would outlast aziS, and the cleaner description is pro-proximal clockwise with aziS immediately downstream of pro.
- Minute numbers are inconsistent across colleagues for aziS, thr, lac, ton, pro and str, and for whether minutes increase clockwise from oriC. The confusion between ~30 min and ~90 min numbering fuels the A/C split.

Unresolved: which map numbering the question adopts and whether the options treat ton and pro as distinct loci or as the same neighbourhood. Options A, C are essentially the same physical requirement – origin immediately upstream of aziS with clockwise transfer – differing only in the label used for the neighbourhood. Option D also maps to an origin upstream of aziS if aziS is placed just counter-clockwise of thr, which is the mirror numbering of the same interval.

Current belief: the logical requirement is clockwise transfer with origin in the pro/ton block immediately upstream of aziS. In the commonly taught 30-40 min numbering this is described as clockwise origin near pro, option C, which is map-isomorphic with option A under the 90 min numbering. The dominant explicit vote in the current pool is C, with A as the same biological class expressed with an alternative label.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The prolonged / early appearance of azis in an interrupted Hfr mating means azis is the first of the scored markers to be entered into the recipient and therefore lies immediately downstream of the Hfr origin of transfer in the direction of transfer.

Map-order claims that keep recurring:

* azi is in the tonB–pro interval, essentially clockwise of tonB and immediately counter-clockwise of pro. In the ~30-40 min numbering thr≈27′, leu≈32-34′, pro≈33-35′, azi≈35-38′, his≈43′. In the ~90-95 min numbering tonB≈89-91′, azi≈92-94′, pro is the same physical block after wrap-around.
* A variant numbering puts azi on the thr→lac arm: thr – … – aziS – … – lac – … – pro – … – str – … – ton – ori. That view makes a lac-proximal origin transferring counter-clockwise meet azi first.
* A third variant puts azi≈27 min, immediately counter-clockwise/up-stream of thr≈28 min. A thr-proximal origin transferring counter-clockwise then meets azi first.

Current round evidence for early-first interpretation:

* Colleagues 10,13,14,16,2,5,7,8,21,1,12 argue the classic pro/ton neighbourhood read out clockwise puts azi essentially at the start of the transfer. An origin just upstream of pro with clockwise transfer gives origin≈pro → aziS → his/arg/lac/ton/str … so azi is the first scored marker and remains expressed for a long window before distal markers.
* Colleagues 11,18,19,20,3,4,15,6 argue the same physical block is described as clockwise origin near ton: origin≈ton → azi → pro → … so azi is the first scored marker after ton. They note ton is often not scored, so azi is effectively first in the assay set.
* Colleagues 1,17, B camp keep the counter-clockwise lac-proximal description: azi lies immediately counter-clockwise of lac, so a lac-proximal origin transferring counter-clockwise meets azi first.
* Colleagues 15,18,3,4, D camp keep the counter-clockwise thr-proximal description: azi is immediately counter-clockwise of thr on their numbering, so a thr-proximal origin transferring counter-clockwise meets azi first.

Conflicts / corrections noticed in this round:

* The exact minute numbers depend on which side of oriC is taken as 0 and on clockwise vs counter-clockwise conventions. The same physical interval is described as “clockwise of ton”, “immediately downstream of pro”, or “counter-clockwise of lac/thr” in different notations.
* If ton is included among the “others”, a clockwise origin exactly at ton would make ton the very first marker and azi the second; the cleanest first-marker statement is obtained when the origin is placed just upstream of azi, i.e. in the pro/ton neighbourhood. Colleague 17 explicitly notes ton-before-azi would make ton the longest-lived marker, which contradicts azi being the prolonged one, favouring the pro-upstream anchor.
* Options A, C and E all describe a clockwise readout from the ton–pro–str neighbourhood; B and D describe a counter-clockwise readout from lac/thr. The bulk of detailed time-of-entry arguments in round 0 and round 1 cluster around a clockwise readout from the pro/ton block with azi being the first of the scored markers after the origin.

Current synthesis: prolonged azis expression = azi is the earliest transferred scored marker. The most commonly cited textbook geometry is the pro/ton neighbourhood read out clockwise, which puts azi essentially at the start of the transfer and therefore gives the long azis window before the more distal lac/thr/str markers appear. In the options as written that is option C, clockwise origin near pro, which is map-isomorphic with option A, clockwise origin near ton, given the adjacency of tonB and pro in the ~30–90 min region. The lac-counter-clockwise and thr-counter-clockwise descriptions are equivalent re-numberings of the same interval but place a different marker first in the ordering.

Unresolved: whether the exam intends the origin to be named “near ton” A or “near pro” C. The majority vote in the current round favours C, with A presented as the same physical Hfr class under the ~90-min numbering. The counter-clockwise B/D options remain minority views in this round.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The time-of-entry logic is unchanged: prolonged/early expression of azis means azis is the first scored marker to be injected and therefore lies immediately downstream of the Hfr origin in the direction of transfer, with all other scored markers arriving later.

The dispute is now almost entirely about map labelling / minute-numbering convention for the pro/ton/azi block, not about the directional logic.

* A-camp / ton-clockwise: Colleagues 11,15,18,19,20,3,4,6 and others keep the classic ~90-95 min numbering tonB ≈89-91 → azi ≈92-94 → str → ori → lac → pro → thr… . On that numbering a clockwise origin in the tonB neighbourhood reads origin → ton → azi → … so azi is the first scored marker to arrive and is expressed for the whole mating, ton being the very first but commonly unscored. They argue option A is the formal description and that C is the same interval re-numbered after wrapping around oriC.

* C-camp / pro-clockwise: Colleagues 1,10,13,14,16,17,2,21,5,7,8,9 now explicitly move to C. They use the teaching 25-40 min numbering thr≈27 → leu≈32 → pro≈33 → azi≈35-38 → his≈43… and read clockwise pro → azi → his… . I have no firm prior yet, but the weight of the current deliberation and the explicit equivalence statements push toward C as the conventionally cited answer, while recognizing A as the same interval under the tonB ~90 min numbering.

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The mechanistic core remains stable across rounds: in an Hfr time-of-entry cross the marker that is expressed for the longest time and appears first is the first scored marker downstream of the F integration site in the direction of transfer. Prolonged aziS/azide expression therefore requires aziS to be the first of the assayed markers after the origin.

The deliberation is still split on map annotation, not on mechanism.

Clockwise pro/ton-proximal camp. Colleagues 1,10,13,14,16,2,21,7,8,5 and in round 1 again 1,10,12,13,14,16 argue azi lies immediately clockwise/downstream of pro, in the ~33-38 min block, with tonB essentially in the same pro/ton neighbourhood. The larger share of round 1 public statements label it C clockwise origin near pro, while a substantial minority label the same block A clockwise origin near ton. With the option wording given, C clockwise origin near pro is the most frequently stated conventional description, with A clockwise origin near ton being its map-isomorphic equivalent.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The time-of-entry signature is first-marker prolonged expression: the gene immediately downstream of the Hfr origin in the direction of transfer is recovered earliest and stays positive longest.

Map-position disagreement is now the whole debate.

* Ton-clockwise camp A: azi/azis is in the ~89-95 min sector, tonB ≈89-91 min → azi ≈92-94 min → str → ori → lac → pro → thr clockwise. An Hfr integrated in the tonB neighbourhood and read clockwise therefore enters ton then azi first, so azi is the first scored marker downstream of the origin and is expressed for a long window before the more distal clockwise markers lac/pro/thr/str are reached. Colleagues 11,18,19,3,4,20,6,15 make this classic Hfr PO/PO2 argument. They note the ton–pro interval is tight and that ton may be un-scored in the set, so azi is the first scored marker.

* Pro-clockwise camp C: the same physical interval is described with the pro numbering ~33 min. Pro ≈33 min → azi ≈35-38 min → his → … clockwise. An Hfr origin just upstream of pro read clockwise gives pro → azi → … so azi is the first selectable marker of the assayed set and remains positive while his/lac/str etc. arrive later. Colleagues 10,13,14,16,21,2,7,8,5,1 now, and 12,17 argue this is the cleaner description because it avoids putting ton in front of azi in the entry order.

* Counter-clockwise / other camps B/D/E are now weakly supported. B lac-counter-clockwise and D thr-counter-clockwise require azi to lie on the thr→lac arm immediately counter-clockwise of lac / upstream of thr, which would make lac/thr the first marker. E str-clockwise is essentially the same ton neighbourhood.

Key points of contention from round 1:
- Whether tonB precedes azi on the clockwise walk. If the origin is truly “near ton” clockwise, ton is entered before azi, so ton should outlast azi unless ton is not scored. 17 and 21 use this to reject A, 11/19/6 use it to accept A with ton unscored.
- Wrap-around naming: pro ~33 min and tonB ~89-91 min are the same region modulo 100 min. Colleagues 15,6,12,1 explicitly state A and C are map-isomorphic descriptions of the ton–pro/azi block; the disagreement is nomenclature / zero of oriC.
- Minute-number confusion persists: some colleagues quote ton ~17/29 min, others ~89-91 min, reflecting different numbering conventions.

Unresolved: exact composition of the “others” scored in the experiment. If ton is part of the scored set, a ton-proximal clockwise origin would make ton the longest-lived marker, not azi. If ton is not scored, azi is the first scored marker for a ton-proximal clockwise Hfr.

Current understanding: the physical requirement is a clockwise read-out from the ton–pro/azi neighbourhood with azi immediately downstream of the origin among the assayed markers. In textbook numbering that is the classic tonB-proximal clockwise Hfr, option A; in the pro numbering used by most of the current round it is described as origin near pro clockwise, option C. B, D, E place azi downstream of an earlier marker in the transfer order and do not give the observed prolonged early azi signal. The debate is effectively A vs C as naming variants of the same ton-pro clockwise block.

15.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The mechanistic read-out is now unanimous across the pool and across rounds: in an Hfr interrupted mating the donor chromosome is injected unidirectionally from the F-integration site; the marker that is entered first is expressed earliest and persists longest. tonB maps in the same pro-ton neighbourhood, a few minutes up- or downstream depending on the zero convention used. With a clockwise Hfr whose integration is placed just upstream of pro the injection order is

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his/arg/lac …

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his/arg/lac…

so that with an origin placed just upstream of pro and transfer proceeding clockwise the entry order is origin ≈ pro → aziS → … . aziS is therefore established essentially at the start of the mating and remains scorable for the whole early phase while his, arg, lac, thr, str and the more distal ton region are only reached later and show progressively shorter windows.

I think we are all describing the same physical Hfr class and the apparent ton vs pro disagreement is really a coordinate-zero issue.

The kinetic we are trying to explain is the classic first-marker effect: in an interrupted Hfr mating the selectable locus that is genetically closest to the origin on the side into which transfer proceeds is entered first and therefore remains phenotypically recoverable for a long window while more distal loci are still being imported. Prolonged azis expression before his/lac/thr/str is exactly that signature.

On the modern K-12 circle the azi/azis interval is mapped immediately downstream of the pro cluster in the clockwise sense: pro ~33 min → azi ~35-38 min → his ~43 min and onward clockwise to lac/thr/ton/str. That is the pro/ton neighbourhood that the older literature quotes as the ~89-94 min ton-azi block. TonB, pro and azi sit in one tight interval and are routinely referred to interchangeably depending on which minute zero and which authors’ map is being used.

With an Hfr integrated just upstream of pro and reading out clockwise the injection order is origin ≈ pro → azi → his … The azi product is made as soon as transfer begins and it stays positive through the early phase of the mating while the more distal clockwise markers are still being pulled in. That is the prolonged early azis window we see, and it is the textbook pro-proximal clockwise Hfr, HfrPO/P O2 type.

Calling the same interval “origin near ton” clockwise is the same geometry written with the older 90-min numbering for the tonB-pro neighbourhood. In the option set as written the conventional, unambiguous anchor for the azi-first block is the pro-proximal clockwise description, i.e. clockwise direction, origin near pro. That is the orientation that makes azi the first scored marker downstream of the origin and accounts naturally for azi being expressed early and for a long time before the downstream markers appear.
public_text.4:
Prolonged early recovery in an interrupted mating is the first-marker effect. The donor is read out unidirectionally from the F integration site and the marker that is the first of the scored set to be encountered downstream of the origin is the one that is made as soon as transfer starts and that stays phenotypically positive while the rest of the chromosome is still being pulled in. A marker that is expressed for a long interval before the others therefore lies immediately downstream of the Hfr origin in the direction of transfer.

On the conventional K-12 clockwise minute map that is used for Hfr time of entry the pro / azi / ton block is contiguous and is read clockwise in the ~30-40 min sector as

thr ≈27 → leu ≈32 → pro ≈33 → azi/azis ≈35-38 → his ≈43 …

tonB is in the same pro-ton neighbourhood and is only a few minutes upstream of pro on the same clockwise walk. With an Hfr origin placed just upstream of pro and transfer proceeding clockwise the read-out is

origin ≃ pro → aziS → his → arg → lac → …

Pro enters first and aziS is the first selectable region encountered after the origin. aziS is therefore established in the recipient at the start of the mating and its product is recoverable for the whole early phase of the mating while the more distal clockwise markers his, arg, lac, thr, str and the more distal ton region are reached later and score for progressively shorter intervals. That is the classic prolonged early aziS window.

A description of the same physical interval as a clockwise ton-proximal origin, option A, is map-isomorphic: tonB ≈89-91 min → azi ≈92-94 min in the alternative ~90 min numbering is the same pro-ton cluster read the other way round the circle. In the conventional teaching nomenclature the interval is cited as a pro-proximal clockwise Hfr, i.e. the classic pro-proximal / HfrPO-type Hfr, which is option C. Origins counter-clockwise near lac, counter-clockwise near thr or clockwise near str would place a different marker, lac/pro/thr/str/ton, immediately downstream of the origin and would make azi a second or later marker, contrary to the observed prolonged early aziS kinetics.

C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro, is the textbook statement of the azi-first Hfr, the same ton-pro block described as A under the 90-min numbering.
public_text.7:
C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

Prolonged early recovery in an interrupted Hfr is the classic first-scored-marker effect: the marker that is genetically closest to the origin on the side into which transfer proceeds is entered first and stays phenotypically positive while the chromosome is pulled in behind it. A long azis window therefore means azis is the first selectable locus of the set to be entered, i.e. it lies immediately downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer.

On the conventional teaching linkage map that is used for Hfr time-of-entry work the pro/azis block is described in the ~30-40 min sector:

thr ~27 → leu ~32 → pro ~33 → aziS ~35-38 → his ~43 → arg/lac …  clockwise

azis is the immediate clockwise neighbour of pro. With an Hfr integrated just upstream of pro and mobilised clockwise the entry order for the scored set is essentially

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his → arg → lac → thr → str …

aziS is therefore established as soon as transfer begins and its product is detectable throughout the early phase of the mating, whereas the more distal clockwise markers are only reached after tens of minutes of transfer and are recovered for progressively shorter intervals. That is the prolonged aziS curve before the later markers appear.

The ton-pro interval is the same physical neighbourhood. TonB maps a few minutes upstream of pro in this numbering and the tonB/pro/azi block is routinely referred to interchangeably as the ton-pro block. In most of the assay sets used for this classic Hfr class tonB itself is not a scored endpoint, so the first selectable marker that is actually seen is aziS. Describing the origin as “near ton” clockwise is a wrap-around description of the same pro-proximal clockwise origin; in the minute numbering used for the options the unambiguous, map-consistent statement is origin near pro, clockwise.

A truly ton-first clockwise read-out would make tonB the first region entered. If tonB were a scored marker it would have to outlast aziS, which is not what is observed. The observed kinetics are therefore most parsimoniously accounted for by the textbook pro-proximal clockwise Hfr that puts aziS first among the scored markers and gives it the long early window relative to his, lac, thr and str. Counter-clockwise lac/thr origins or a str-proximal clockwise origin would place aziS several minutes downstream of the first entered marker and cannot give aziS the earliest, longest-lived phenotype.

That is option C, clockwise transfer initiated in the pro/ton neighbourhood with aziS immediately downstream of the origin.

The kinetic requirement is fixed: prolonged early expression = the first scored marker downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer. Transfer is unidirectional, so the first marker encountered is made as soon as transfer starts and stays phenotypically positive for the whole time course, later markers appearing sequentially and for progressively shorter windows.

On the teaching linkage map that is used for time-of-entry work aziS/azis is essentially the first selectable locus clockwise of the pro cluster

thr ~27 → leu ~32 → pro ~33 → azi ~35-38 → his ~43 → …

going clockwise from oriC.  TonB sits in the same pro/ton neighbourhood, a few minutes upstream of azi in this numbering.  With a clockwise Hfr whose integration site is placed just upstream of pro the injection order is

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his/arg/lac/str/ton …

pro is the first donor DNA to arrive and aziS follows essentially immediately after it. In any marker set that does not score pro as the primary endpoint, aziS is therefore the first scored marker to be entered and it is recovered for the long early window while the more distal clockwise markers are still being pulled in. That is the classic prolonged azis-before-others curve.

An origin described as “near ton” with clockwise readout is the map-isomorphic description of the same pro/ton block under the alternative 90-min numbering where tonB≈89-91 min → azi≈92-94 min. In that numbering tonB is in principle upstream of azi in the clockwise entry order, so tonB would be the first marker and would outlast azi if tonB were scored. The statement that azi is the prolonged early marker is therefore most cleanly and unambiguously stated with the conventionally taught anchor, origin just upstream of azi i.e. pro-proximal, read clockwise.

That is the clockwise pro-proximal Hfr, option C. Option A. Clockwise origin near ton is the same physical ton/pro/azi neighbourhood expressed with the 90-min numbering, which is why the two descriptions are used interchangeably in the literature. The lac-counter-clockwise, thr-counter-clockwise and str-clockwise options would place intervening selectable loci ahead of azi in the entry order and cannot give azi the earliest, longest-lived phenotype.

Prolonged azis is the classic first-marker signature in an interrupted Hfr time-of-entry. The marker that is closest to the origin on the side that is first transferred is made as soon as transfer starts and remains phenotypically scorable for the whole early phase of the mating, while more distal markers are only recovered later and for a progressively shorter window.

In the map numbering that is used for Hfr mapping and for the options here the azis/azi interval sits immediately downstream of the pro cluster in the clockwise sense. The conventional teaching order in that neighbourhood is pro ~33 min → azi ~35-38 min → his ~43 min and onward clockwise to lac/thr/ton/str. With a clockwise Hfr whose integration is just upstream of pro the injection order is origin ≈ pro → azi → his → arg → lac …

Azis is therefore established essentially as soon as transfer begins and it stays positive through the early part of the mating while the more distal clockwise markers are still being pulled in. That is exactly the long early azis window followed by the later, shorter windows for his, lac, thr, str etc.

The “origin near ton clockwise” description is the same physical ton-pro block referred to with a different zero convention. On the 89-95 min numbering that block is tonB → azi → pro, which makes tonB the first chromosomal region encountered on a clockwise read-out from a ton-proximal origin. If the origin were truly tonB-proximal clockwise, tonB would be entered before azi and ton-associated phenotypes should be the ones with the prolonged early window, not azis. The experiment shows azis as the prolonged early marker, not ton.

That is why the pro-anchored description is the cleanest one in the options: a clockwise origin placed just upstream of pro puts azi as the first selectable marker of the set to be entered in the direction of transfer, giving the observed prolonged azis expression before the downstream clockwise markers appear. B, D and E place azi several minutes downstream of the first entered marker or on the opposite side of the origin and cannot give azi the earliest, longest-lived phenotype.

The prolonged aziS window is the textbook first-marker signature in an interrupted Hfr: the gene that is entered first is the one that is phenotypically positive earliest and stays positive the longest while the chromosome is fed in downstream of it.

That means aziS has to be the first selectable region to be encountered after the integration site in the direction of transfer. In the conventional teaching linkage map that is used for Hfr time-of-entry work the order in this block is read clockwise as

pro ~33 min → azi/azis ~35-38 min → his ~43 min → …

with tonB sitting in the same pro-ton cluster a few minutes upstream of pro in that numbering. aziS is therefore immediately clockwise/downstream of pro and is the first selectable marker that is met on a clockwise read-out from a pro-proximal origin.

With an origin placed just upstream of pro and transfer proceeding clockwise the entry order is

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his/arg/lac/thr/str …

aziS is established essentially as soon as transfer begins and its product is detectable for the whole early phase of the mating, whereas his, lac, thr, str and the more distal ton region are only reached later and have progressively shorter recovery windows. That is exactly the prolonged early aziS expression before the later markers become detectable.

The ton-pro neighbourhood is the same physical interval on the circle; the minute numbers ~89-94 min for ton/azi are just the same block with a different oriC zero. In that alternative numbering an origin described as “near ton” clockwise is map-isomorphic to a pro-proximal clockwise origin. On the labeling used in the options the conventional statement of the early azi block is the clockwise, pro-proximal Hfr, i.e. origin near pro clockwise, option C.

Calling the origin “near ton” clockwise is the source of the confusion. If the origin were truly tonB-proximal in the clockwise sense, tonB would be the first chromosomal DNA entered and, in a strictly linear unidirectional transfer, the first entered region should be the longest lived. The data show aziS as the prolonged early marker, not ton. The cleanest reading is that aziS is the first scored marker downstream of the origin, which is the pro → azi clockwise order most groups teach for the classic HfrPO/HfrPO2 type Hfr. That is option C.

In an interrupted Hfr time of entry the marker that is first encountered downstream of the F integration site in the direction of mobilisation is the one that is recovered earliest and whose phenotype persists the longest, because it is made as soon as transfer begins and stays in the ex-conjugant while the donor chromosome is read out linearly behind it.

Prolonged azis/azide expression therefore means azis is the first selectable marker of the set that is entered, i.e. azis lies essentially immediately downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer.

On the conventional K-12 clockwise linkage that underlies the classic Hfr time-of-entry maps the pro/ton/azi block is read clockwise as

thr ≈27 → leu ≈32 → pro ≈33 → azi/azis ≈35-38 → his ≈43 → ...

tonB maps in the same pro-ton neighbourhood a few minutes upstream of azi. With an Hfr integration just upstream of pro and mobilisation clockwise the injection order is

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his/arg/lac…

pro is the first DNA that enters and aziS follows essentially immediately after it. aziS is therefore phenotypically established at the very start of the mating and remains scorable for the whole early phase, whereas his, arg, lac, thr, str and the more distal ton markers are reached later and are only recovered for progressively shorter windows. That is the classic first-marker, long-lived azi signal.

A nominal “origin near ton, clockwise” is the same pro/ton physical interval described with the alternative minute numbering in which the tonB-azi region is numbered ~89-94 min. In that numbering tonB would be the very first DNA to enter and would be expected to outlast aziS. The conventional, unambiguous anchor for the first scored marker being aziS is the pro-proximal clockwise Hfr, i.e. origin near pro read clockwise. In the option wording this is

C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

which is the map-isomorphic description of the classic pro/ton clockwise Hfr that makes azi the first scored marker and accounts for its prolonged early expression before the downstream markers appear.

The prolonged early recovery of azis is the textbook first-marker effect in an interrupted Hfr: the marker that is entered first is the one that is made as soon as transfer starts and stays phenotypically positive while the chromosome is read out downstream.

On the teaching K-12 circular map the azis/azide resistance block is in the pro/ton neighbourhood and it is consistently placed immediately downstream of pro on a clockwise read-out. In the 30-40 min numbering that is most commonly used for Hfr time-of-entry work this is

pro ~33 min → azi ~35-38 min → his ~43 min → … → lac/thr/str further clockwise

so that with an origin placed just upstream of pro and transfer proceeding clockwise the entry order is origin ≈ pro → aziS → … . aziS is therefore established essentially at the start of the mating and remains scorable for the whole early phase while his, arg, lac, thr, str and the more distal ton region are only reached later and show progressively shorter windows.

TonB does lie in the same pro/ton cluster, a few minutes upstream of azi in the 90-min numbering. That is why the same physical Hfr class is sometimes described as ton-proximal clockwise. In the scored set used here tonB is not a selectable endpoint, so aziS is in practice the first scored marker to be delivered after the origin. The ton/azi/pro block is contiguous, the minute numbers are simply a wrap-around convention ~30-40 min vs ~89-94 min, and the pro label is the more precise anchor for the interval that places azi immediately downstream of the origin in the clockwise direction.

A clockwise origin in the pro neighbourhood therefore makes azi the first and longest-lived scored marker, giving the observed prolonged azis expression before the later clockwise markers appear. A true lac-proximal counter-clockwise, thr-proximal counter-clockwise or str-proximal clockwise orientation would place a different marker ahead of azi in the entry order and cannot give azi the earliest, most persistent signal.

That is the classic pro-proximal clockwise Hfr, the C description of the pro/ton azi-first block.

Prolonged recovery in an interrupted mating is the first-marker effect: the locus that is first encountered downstream of the integrated F origin in the direction of transfer is established as soon as transfer starts and it stays phenotypically recoverable while the chromosome is pulled in behind it. Distal loci are only recovered after the transfer front has reached them and therefore have progressively shorter windows.

On the map that is normally used for Hfr time-of-entry work aziS/azis is the immediate clockwise neighbour of the pro cluster, pro → aziS → … in the clockwise sense. In the conventional teaching numbering that is

pro ≈33 min  → azi ≈35-38 min → his ≈43 min → … 

with tonB lying in the same pro/ton neighbourhood a few minutes further clockwise. With an Hfr whose integration site is placed just upstream of pro and which is mobilised clockwise the injection order is

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his/arg/lac etc.

so aziS is essentially the first selectable chromosomal marker to be injected. Its product is made as soon as transfer begins and its phenotype is therefore recovered for a long early interval, whereas the more distal clockwise markers his, lac, thr, str and the ton region are reached later and are scored only for a progressively shorter part of the time course.

That is the classic pro-proximal clockwise Hfr, the Hfr PO/Hfr PO2 type that gives the early, persistent azi signal followed by the later downstream markers. The same physical interval is often quoted in the older ~90 min numbering as a ton-proximal clockwise origin – the ton-pro block is the same pro/ton neighbourhood – and in that numbering system it is described as option A. In the minute numbering used for the options the unambiguous first-downstream description is the clockwise, pro-proximal origin, option C, i.e. the clockwise pro/ton azi-first Hfr.

A counter-clockwise origin near lac/thr/str, or a clockwise origin near str/ton with ton scored before azi, would put an intervening selectable marker ahead of aziS in the entry order and aziS would not be the first and longest-lived marker in the kinetics.
