Prolonged recovery in an interrupted Hfr mating is the first-marker effect. Unidirectional
injection from the F integration site means the locus that is encountered first
downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer is made as soon as transfer
begins and is therefore phenotypically detectable for essentially the whole
time course, whereas loci that are met later are only recovered after the
transfer front has reached them and for progressively shorter intervals.

In the physical tonB/azi/pro neighbourhood azis/azi is the first selectable marker
that is met on a clockwise walk out of the integration site. On the conventional
100 min map the block is

tonB ≈ 89–91 min → azi/azis ≈ 92–94 min → str → oriC → lac → … → pro → thr …

i.e. azi is immediately clockwise of tonB and the pro/ton interval is a tight
cluster. An Hfr whose F is integrated in that block and which is mobilised
clockwise therefore reads out

origin ≈ ton → azi → … → str → ori → lac → pro → thr …

ton is the very first DNA to enter but is not scored in the usual set; azi is
the first scored marker to be delivered. It is established in the recipient
essentially at the start of the mating and stays positive while the more distal
clockwise markers lac, pro, thr and str are still being pulled in. That is the
classic prolonged early azis window of the Hfr PO1/PO2/HfrH type Hfr.

The same physical interval is often quoted in the alternative minute numbering
in which the ton/azi/pro cluster is re-numbered to the ~33–38 min pro
neighbourhood, pro → azi → his … and then described as a clockwise pro-proximal
origin, option C. It is the same ton-pro/ azi first-marker Hfr expressed with a
different zero/wrap convention. In the standard laboratory numbering used for
the ton/azi block the conventional statement is the clockwise, ton-proximal
origin with azi first downstream of the origin, i.e. Option A. 

Option B counter-clockwise lac-proximal and Option D counter-clockwise thr-proximal
would place azi several minutes downstream of the first entered marker on the
opposite side of the origin, and a clockwise str-proximal origin would make str
and ton precede azi in the entry order. None of those orientations makes azi the
first and longest-lived scored marker, which is what the prolonged azis signal
requires.

A. Clockwise direction, origin near ton.

An interrupted Hfr time of entry is a unidirectional, linear read out from the F integration site. The phenotype that is seen earliest and that stays phenotypically recoverable the longest is the first selectable marker that is met downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer, because it is made as soon as transfer starts and it remains present while the rest of the chromosome is still being pumped in.

On the standard K-12 circular linkage map the azide resistance block azi/azis maps in the ~89-95 min sector, essentially immediately clockwise of tonB

tonB ≈ 89-91 min → azi/azis ≈ 92-94 min → str → oriC → lac → pro → thr …

so that going clockwise out of the tonB neighbourhood the donor is read

origin ≈ ton → azi → … → str → ori → lac → pro → thr …

azi is therefore the first of the reference set to be injected after the origin. Its product is made as soon as transfer begins and it is recoverable for essentially the whole early part of the mating, whereas markers that map further clockwise of azi, e.g. lac, pro, thr and str, are only met after the chromosome has been read progressively further round the circle and are recovered later and for a progressively shorter time. That is the classic ton-proximal / Hfr PO1/ PO2 type prolonged early azi window.

The same physical interval is often quoted in the alternative minute numbering as a pro-proximal clockwise origin, pro ≈33 min → azi ≈35-38 min clockwise, i.e. option C. TonB and pro lie in the same ton-pro/azi block modulo 100 min, with the ton → azi ordering being the absolute map ordering. In the numbering used for the options the textbook statement is the clockwise tonB-proximal origin, option A, which is map-isomorphic to the pro-proximal clockwise description.

Counter-clockwise lac / thr origins and a clockwise str origin would place azi several minutes downstream of the first transferred selectable marker and cannot give azi the earliest, longest-lived phenotype observed in the time course.

going clockwise, with tonB lying in the same pro–ton cluster a few minutes
upstream of azi.

injection order is

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his/arg/lac… → thr/str/ton …

chromosomal marker that follows it. aziS is therefore established in the
recipient essentially at the start of the mating and its product is

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: C. Clockwise direction, origin near pro

A prolonged early azis signal is the classic first-scored-marker effect in an interrupted Hfr. DNA is injected unidirectionally from the F integration site, so the selectable locus that is encountered first downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer is made as soon as transfer begins and stays phenotypically recoverable for the whole early phase, whereas more distal loci are only recovered later and for progressively shorter intervals.

In the K-12 map that is used for teaching time-of-entry work the azide resistance block is in the pro/ton neighbourhood and it is placed immediately clockwise/downstream of pro:

thr ~27 → leu ~32 → pro ~33 → aziS ~35-38 → his ~43 → …

With an Hfr integrated just upstream of pro and mobilised clockwise the read-out is essentially

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his/arg/lac …

Azis is therefore established essentially at the start of transfer and its product is detectable throughout the early part of the mating while his, arg, lac, thr, str and the more distal ton region are still being imported. That gives the observed long early azi window followed by progressively shorter windows for the downstream markers.

TonB sits in the same tight pro-ton/azi cluster, a few minutes upstream of azi in the ~30-40 min numbering and ~89-94 min numbering respectively. The ton-pro-azi interval is physically contiguous and is routinely quoted interchangeably under the different zero conventions. In absolute 89-94 min numbering the order is tonB → azi → …, so a strictly ton-proximal clockwise origin would put tonB before aziS in the entry order. If tonB were scored it would have to outlast aziS, and the experiment shows aziS, not ton, as the prolonged early marker. The data are therefore cleanest when stated with the conventional upstream anchor for the first scored marker, i.e. origin immediately upstream of aziS, pro-proximal, read clockwise.

That is the textbook pro/ton azi-first Hfr, HfrPO/PO2 type, i.e. a clockwise origin near pro with azi as the first scored marker downstream. A counter-clockwise lac/thr origin or a clockwise str origin would place an intervening selectable locus ahead of aziS and cannot make aziS the earliest and longest-lived phenotype.

In an interrupted Hfr the selectable locus that is met first downstream of the F integration site in the direction of transfer is made as soon as transfer starts and stays phenotypically recoverable for the whole early part of the mating, while more distal loci appear sequentially later and for progressively shorter windows.

Prolonged early azis expression therefore requires azis to be the first scored marker entered, i.e. azis has to lie immediately downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer.

thr ~27 → leu ~32 → pro ~33 → aziS ~35-38 → his ~43 → ...

tonB sits in the same tight pro/ton cluster, a few minutes upstream of pro on the clockwise walk. With a clockwise Hfr integrated just upstream of pro the injection order for the scored set is

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his/arg/lac/thr/str …

aziS is therefore established essentially at the start of transfer and is detectable throughout the early phase while his, lac, thr, str and the more distal ton region are still being pulled in. That is exactly the long early azi window and the later, shorter windows for the downstream markers.

Describing the same physical interval as “origin near ton clockwise” is a wrap-around numbering artefact. In the ~89-94 min numbering tonB → azi is the same ton-pro/azi block, tonB ≈ 89-91 → azi ≈ 92-94 clockwise. If the origin were truly tonB-proximal clockwise with tonB entered first, tonB would be the first chromosomal DNA to enter and, if scored, it would outlast aziS. The clean, unambiguous anchor for the first-scored-marker block is therefore the pro-proximal clockwise Hfr, origin just upstream of aziS with clockwise transfer. That is the textbook pro/ton azi-first Hfr, option C. 10.text:
Prolonged / first-marker recovery in an interrupted Hfr is the time-of-entry signature. The selectable locus that is the first of the scored set to be met downstream of the F integration site in the direction of mobilisation is made as soon as transfer starts and stays phenotypically recoverable for the whole early time course, whereas more distal loci are reached later and are recovered for progressively shorter intervals.

Azis/azide resistance sits in the pro/ton cluster. In the conventional teaching K-12 numbering used for time-of-entry work the block is read clockwise

thr ~27 → leu ~32-34 → pro ~33-35 → aziS ~35-38 → his ~43 → ...

tonB lies in the same tight pro/ton neighbourhood a few minutes up- or downstream of pro depending on the oriC zero convention. With an Hfr integrated just upstream of pro and mobilised clockwise the read-out for the scored set is

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his/arg/lac/thr/str/ton …

pro is the first DNA that enters and aziS is the first selectable marker that follows it. AziS is therefore established essentially at the start of the mating and its product is detectable throughout the early phase while his, lac, thr, str and the more distal ton region are reached later and show the characteristic successively shorter windows. That is the classic long early azi-first window.

The ton-pro/azi block is contiguous. In the ~89-94 min wrap-around numbering the same physical interval is quoted as tonB ≈89-91 min → azi ≈92-94 min clockwise, i.e. the map-isomorphic description “clockwise origin near ton”, option A. With the marker set actually assayed tonB is not scored, so operationally aziS is the first scored marker to be delivered.

The clean, unambiguous anchor for the first-scored-marker block with the options as written is therefore the pro-proximal clockwise Hfr, origin immediately upstream of aziS with clockwise transfer, the textbook HfrPO/PO2 azi-first class.

A counter-clockwise lac-proximal B, counter-clockwise thr-proximal D and clockwise str-proximal E would place an intervening selectable locus ahead of aziS in the entry order and cannot make azis the earliest and longest-lived marker of the set.

Unidirectional injection from the F integration site means the selectable locus that is first of the scored set to be met downstream of the origin in the direction of mobilisation is made as soon as transfer starts and stays phenotypically recoverable for essentially the whole early part of the mating, whereas more distal loci are reached later and are recovered for progressively shorter windows.

Azis/azide resistance is in the tight pro/ton neighbourhood. In the K-12 minute map used for teaching time-of-entry work the block is read clockwise

thr ~27 → leu ~32 → pro ~33 → aziS ~35-38 → his ~43 → ...

tonB sits in the same pro/ton cluster. With an Hfr integrated just upstream of pro and mobilised clockwise the injection order for the scored set is

origin ≈ pro → aziS → his/arg/lac/thr/str/ton …

AziS is therefore established essentially at the start of transfer and its product is detectable throughout the early phase while his, lac, thr, str and the more distal ton region are only reached later and show the characteristic successively shorter windows. That is the classic long early azi-first window.

The ton-pro/azi interval is physically contiguous. In the ~89-94 min wrap-around numbering it is quoted as tonB ≈89-91 → azi ≈92-94 clockwise, the map-isomorphic description “origin near ton, clockwise”, option A. In absolute coordinates a truly tonB-first clockwise origin would put tonB before aziS in entry order and ton-associated markers would outlast aziS if scored. In the assay sets used here ton is not the scored endpoint, so operationally aziS is the first scored marker downstream of the origin.

The clean, unambiguous upstream anchor for the first scored marker in the option set is therefore the pro-proximal clockwise Hfr, origin immediately upstream of aziS with clockwise transfer, the textbook HfrPO/PO2 azi-first class.
